# Goeteia

> Goeteia is a self-hosting Scheme that compiles to WebAssembly GC (and
> to plain JavaScript), with a web and graphics toolkit written in the
> same language: DOM, CSS, reactive state, WebGL/GLSL and glTF are all
> Scheme libraries, so a whole page — markup, interaction, 3D — is one
> program in one language and no JavaScript is written by hand. The
> compiler, the prelude and the runtime ship in one npm package; Node
> 22+ is the only prerequisite.

`docs/llm/` is a substrate meant to be **injected as context**: it is
written for a model that has never seen this language and has to emit a
page that compiles and runs the first time. `manifest.json` says which
layers to include for a given kind of page, and what each one costs in
bytes. Each tier document is built around one complete program, and the
test suite compiles that program, runs it, judges it, and asserts the
document carries the source byte for byte — so what is shown is what
was verified.

## The page substrate (inject these)

- [Core](docs/llm/core.md): the shape of every page — the `.ss` IS the browser half, its two hosts (`#app`, `#c`), the whole `(web dom)` vocabulary, which imports a task needs, and the DO/DON'T table for the traps that actually bite. Always include this one.
- [Manifest](docs/llm/manifest.json): which layers to inject for which task, the byte cost of each combination, and the check spec each example is verified against.
- [T1 — a static page](docs/llm/t1-static.md): building elements into `#app`, `set-inner-html!` versus real elements, stylesheets through `(web css)`.
- [T2 — an interactive page](docs/llm/t2-interactive.md): creating and wiring controls, the `js->number` fixnum trap at the JS boundary, rounding.
- [T3 — meshes in three dimensions](docs/llm/t3-mesh3d.md): `fx-init!` on the canvas the page already has, `fx-program!` from shader forms, the `(gfx mesh)` generators, column-major mat4s.
- [T4 — a fragment shader](docs/llm/t4-shader.md): `glsl->string` as a pure function, float literals, reserved words refused at generation time, `fx-fullscreen!`.
- [T5 — an articulated, animated scene](docs/llm/t5-animated.md): a rig as a chain of `m4-mul` frames, controls and animation in one program.

## Reference

- [Manual](README.md): the whole language and library reference — syntax, the standard procedures, `(web *)`, `(gfx *)`, the mount-point family, and the build model.
- [Verifying a page](docs/verify.md): `goeteia verify` and `goeteia pack` — the four stages (compile, smoke, draw, interact), the check-spec schema, and the mock world a page is judged in.
- [Numeric limits and traps](docs/limits.md): the i31 fixnum range, what the reader does and does not accept, the shader and staging capacities.
- [Graphics](docs/graphics.md): the `(gfx *)` libraries in depth.
- [Numeric determinism](docs/determinism.md): which equalities across hosts, targets and optimization levels the language guarantees.
- [The JavaScript backend](docs/js-backend.md): the `--js` target and how it mirrors the wasm one.

## Optional

- [Examples](examples/): 46 standalone programs, each runnable with `goeteia <file.ss>`, several with a page to open beside them.
- [Tests](test/): the suite, including the page fixtures in `test/pages/` whose verdicts are known.
